bib.title: Efficient Transformers: A Survey
bib.venue: preprint (arXiv v3, Mar 2022; ledger lists ACM Comput. Surv. 2023)

question: How can the many efficiency-oriented X-former variants be organised, and what trends and gaps do they show?
contributions: A taxonomy of efficient Transformers by core technique (fixed patterns, combination, learnable patterns, neural memory, low-rank, kernels, recurrence, downsampling, sparse/MoE).
Table 1 summarising complexity, decoder support and class for about 30 models.
Walk-through of representative models, discussion of evaluation, design trends and a V2 retrospective.

results.claim: Self-attention costs quadratic time and memory in sequence length; the QK^T product alone is N^2.
results.quote:
In particular, the QK⊤matrix multiplication operation
alone consumes N2 time and memory.

results.claim: The feed-forward layers take roughly half the compute of a Transformer block, so attention-only efficiency leaves much cost.
results.setup: Standard Transformer block; stated without measurement
results.quote: (approximately half the compute time and/or FLOPs)

results.claim: Block pruning is reported to make a Transformer 2.4x faster with little loss on language tasks.
results.setup: Lagunas et al. (2021) block pruning, language tasks
results.quote: can make a Transformer 2.4x faster with little loss in predictive performance on language tasks

results.claim: Linear Transformers are reported to speed inference up to three orders of magnitude without much loss in predictive performance.
results.quote: improve inference speeds up to three orders of magnitude without much loss in predictive performance

results.claim: Linear-attention models struggle to be competitive on common benchmarks, and none of the xformer variants became the de facto standard.
results.setup: Retrospective as of Dec 2021, citing Xiong et al. 2021a
results.quote:
linear attention (e.g., Performer) models struggle to be competitive on common
benchmarks

results.claim: Causal (unidirectional) kernel attention can be several times slower than vanilla Transformer in parallel teacher-forced training because of the left-to-right scan.
results.quote:
can be several
times slower than vanilla Transformer during parallelized training

results.claim: Local attention done right is a tough baseline to beat for long-context tasks.
results.quote:
local attention, when done right, can be a really
tough baseline to beat

results.claim: Efficient-attention models are not always faster: lower complexity can be slower in practice, and linear models give no gain at short lengths.
results.quote: A model of linear complexity can be slower than a model with quadratic complexity in practice.

results.claim: Models are not comparable: each paper picks its own benchmarks and sizes; Long Range Arena benchmarked 10 xformer variants on encoder-only tasks.
results.setup: Tay et al. 2021a LRA; no causal/autoregressive tasks
results.quote:
benchmarked 10 diﬀerent xformer
variants on long range modeling tasks

results.claim: Memory-compressed attention cost falls to O(n*n/k) with strided convolution of kernel and stride k; blockwise local attention is O(b*n).
results.quote:
the computational
and memory cost of the attention mechanism reduces to O(n · n/k)

limits: Survey only: no experiments of its own and no head-to-head numbers.
Authors concede there is no easy way to compare models because papers pick their own benchmarks, sizes and sometimes conflate with pretraining (Sec 4.1).
Complexity does not equal wall-clock speed; many variants are slower or lack causal masking / TPU packing (Sec 4.4).
Dated: covers to early 2022; predates FlashAttention-style IO-aware exact attention and modern long-context LLMs.
practices: Distinguish memory complexity from real throughput before adopting an efficient-attention variant (footnote 1, Sec 4.4).
Treat local/windowed attention as the strong baseline for long-context tasks (Sec 4.4, citing Xiong et al. 2021a).
If sequence length varies, sequentially processing the input may suffice instead of an approximation (Sec 4.4, citing Rabe and Staats 2021).
Check that an efficient attention supports causal masking before using it for autoregressive generation (Sec 2.5, 3.2.7, 3.2.8).
Compare encoder-only models only with encoder-only benchmarks such as Long Range Arena (Sec 4.1).

terms.definition: this class of models [variants addressing the quadratic cost of self-attention]
sparsifies the attention matrix by limiting the field of view to fixed, predefined patterns such as local windows and block patterns of fixed strides
learn the access pattern in a data-driven fashion, assigning tokens to buckets or clusters
a learnable side memory module that can access multiple tokens at once, e.g. global tokens or inducing points
assume low-rank structure in the N x N attention matrix, e.g. Linformer projecting length N to k
view attention through kernelization to avoid explicitly computing the N x N matrix
connects blocks via segment-level recurrence, as in Transformer-XL
reduce the resolution of the sequence, reducing computation by a commensurate factor
sparsely activate a subset of the parameters, improving the parameter to FLOPs ratio (MoE)
